topic: What if your shadow could move on its own?
title: WHAT IF YOUR SHADOW
MOVED ON ITS OWN?

power.rule: your shadow stands up off the wall and acts for you, on your command
power.look: the picture sinks a stop while the DETACH chip blinks; the silhouette's edge ripples as it peels off

script.text: Detach. Your shadow fetches the remote.
Detach. It flips the light off across the room.
Detach. It waves at Mo without being asked.
What if your shadow could move on its own?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch: your shadow's just a hole in the light. On the Moon, its edge sweeps by at thirteen times light speed. That's real.
So where does it go at night?

science.claim: On the Moon, a shadow's edge sweeps by at thirteen times the speed of light.
science.working: A tight beam behind you projects your silhouette onto the Moon (mean distance 384,400 km = 3.844e8 m). A quick wrist flick sweeps about 1 radian in 0.1 s, so the angle rate omega = 10 rad/s. The spot's edge moves at v = r * omega = 3.844e8 m * 10 rad/s = 3.84e9 m/s = 3.84e9 / 2.998e8 ≈ 12.8c. A quicker flick (0.05 s per radian) gives about 26c; 0.1 s is the conservative read, so 'thirteen times light speed' holds.
science.source: NASA (mean Earth-Moon distance: 384,400 km); special relativity — the speed limit applies to matter and information; a shadow is the absence of photons, a spot that carries none, so no limit

science.claim: Your shadow is just a hole in the light — not a thing.
science.working: A shadow is the region the rays no longer reach: no photons, no mass, no energy of its own (weight 0). It exists only where a light source and a blocker agree.
science.source: Physics of shadows: an absence of photons, not an object

shots.note: night, lamp on: Pip sits up in bed and points at the dresser; the DETACH chip blinks
his black silhouette peels off the floor and walks toward the dresser under the window
the shadow's mitten lifts the remote off the dresser among the plant and the speaker
the shadow reaches the nightstand lamp and pulls it dark; the room falls to moonlight
Mo leans in at the lit doorway waving; the shadow on the floor waves back first
Pip, uneasy in the moonlight, looks from the wave to Mo
the title over Pip and his shadow standing side by side on the moonlit floor
A SHADOW IS A HOLE IN THE LIGHT: rays part around a blocker icon; NO PHOTONS, NO MASS
the beam lands on the Moon, 384,400 km; a hand flick sweeps 1 radian in 0.1 s; the counter climbs to 12.8x light speed
That's real: Pip, worried, the rims cooling toward red
the shadow, taller now, waves on its own behind still Pip, then walks out through the door and fades into the hall light
